title: Whitelight Triage Card — prioritized retry guidance & payload snapshot
creator: Marisol Gomez
description: Design a compact, embeddable triage card (Whitelight) for the Redwood Console that surfaces a prioritized list of failed requests, suggested retry strategies, and a condensed payload snapshot. The card is intended for both high-density dashboards and route-level pages to accelerate first-touch debugging without leaving the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Card renders in list/dense modes at 3 widths (full, half, compact) with readable payload snapshot
Primary error taxonomy tag is derived from server-side classifier and displayed with confidence score
Suggested retry action (manual retry / exponential backoff / escalate) is computed and shown with rationale
Clicking 'Inspect payload' opens an inline modal with key/value diffs and KV cache hints
Telemetry hooks present for click-throughs, retry attempts, and time-to-first-action metrics
decisions: Embed condensed payload (top 6 keys) rather than full request body to reduce noise and cost for large payloads
Prioritize errors by a computed signal: weighted score of frequency, latency impact, and user-facing rate
Default suggested action order: safe-retry (idempotent) -> backoff-retry -> escalate, with policy override for sensitive routes
tradeoffs: Showing only top keys can hide root cause but keeps the card lightweight for dashboards
Automated retry suggestions risk encouraging retries for non-idempotent operations; mitigated by clear labeling and policy gating
In-dashboard diff/inspect increases Console latency slightly; will lazy-load full payload only on demand
review_comments: Rohit Patel (Eng): 'Love the compact approach. Need a strict flag for non-idempotent routes — otherwise platform might suggest unsafe retries.'
Leah Rosen (PM): 'Add a quick link to the rollout history for the model/version implicated in the errors — helps correlate regressions.'
Samir Khan (SRE): 'Ensure we surface throttle vs. model-error distinction. Suggested color coding for telemetry.'
Avery Chen (Design): 'Prototype v2 updated to include confidence glyph and policy badge; see Figma frames 14-19.'
